entries.value: verb-final (SOV); the verb closes the clause
after the noun: suffixed postpositions (-te in/at/to/from) and free postpositions (namba with, mokho-te inside, zita-te after)
possessor before the possessed; the possessive suffix agrees with the possessed noun: -qa (things), -ge (a man), -gu (a woman), -gi (plural)

pronoun series by person and by class of the possessed: noqa/noge/nogu/nogi (my), qoqa/qoge/qogu/qogi (your sg), teqa/tege/tegu/tegi (his), tuqa/tuge/tugu/tugi (her), niqa/nigi (our), zoqa/zogi (your pl), tiqa/tigi (their); ekeza = own (reflexive)
no article; demonstratives instead: ngenek (this man), ngunuk (this woman), nginik (these people), nqanek (this thing), 'ta X ndøgo' (that X)
no (I), qo (you sg), ndego (he), ndugu (she), ni (we), zo (you pl), ndigu (they)
narrative-past subject prefixes on the verb: ge- (he), gu- (she), gi- (they), qa- (it); gu- also appears when the object is a woman and the subject a man; a plural subject wins over a feminine object
entries.note: The gender reading of gu- is the agent's hypothesis (notes, open question 10); a speaker should confirm.

entries.value: object prefixes inside the verb: mbo-/mbøe- (him/her), zø-/zømbe- (them, you pl), nø- (me), ni- (us), qa-/taqa- (you sg); a free noun object often takes no prefix
directionals inside the verb: -nø- thither (away), -ndo-/-ndu- hither (towards the centre)
narrative past with ndø- (neutral), mø̀ndø- (perfective, 'has already'), gè- (completed), te-/tu-/ti- + ne/ni (emphatic past)
future marked by a high tone on the stem; the same consonants as the past
subordinate / conditional / 'that' clauses take irrealis prefixes: tæ- (I), toqo-/toqote- (you), te- (he), tu- (she), ti- (they), tozo- (you pl), tizi- (we); 'even if' = 'Oskiá ndøgo, …'
negative suffix on the verb: -áv / -eáv / -teáv (past), -ák (future); 'there is none / without' = mbaín after the noun
prohibition by a tone pattern on the verb: grave on the penult and the rising mark (U+1DC4) on the last vowel, object prefix kept
commands: 2sg and 2pl forms with their own prefixes (mò-/qa- sg; tozo-/sozó-/zøtø- pl), 1pl hortative bizi-
wishes and blessings with the prefix be-/bezø- ('may he …', 'may it be for them')
the frame precedes the quote: speaker, (addressee), 'said thus' with the subject prefix, then the quote in double quotes; a short frame is the verb with the object prefix alone
reported content and perception with 'av nqægo, …' and macron tones on the content verb
entries.pattern: <verb of saying/hearing/seeing>, av nqægo, <content with macron tones>

entries.value: “ ” for direct speech, ‘ ’ inside a quote
a vocative stands first as its own sentence with a full stop or exclamation mark
polar questions open with 'Gê,' and carry a circumflex on the last word; 'why' = 'Gekha zapâ, …'; 'who' = gekha ezoqâm
a locative relative is bracketed 'ma … ndøgo' (where …); the clause precedes its head

'Yaq' opens most narrative sentences (then, and so); on the verb the prefix vø̄- chains a following action without subject marking; 'neka' joins nouns and clauses; 'Geté' = but; 'Zapa ndǿgo,' = because; 'Yaq nakémbá.' = therefore; 'atema' = until

many short sentences: one BSB sentence often becomes two or three; a name or an attribute stands as its own sentence; a place phrase is often set off after the verb; a predicate noun or adjective ends in a high tone
a time setting opens the sentence: 'Ta khøuwa-te ndøgo, …' (in those days), 'Khøuwa nøme,' (one day), 'Taqa zita-te,' (afterwards)
'X's name was Y' as '<X>-qa iz, <Y>.' with a high tone on the name; 'their names' = tiqa iziz; naming = 'iz <Y> mbo-akhaém'; 'his name shall be Y' = 'Teqa iz <Y> ndǿgoát'
'there was' = mø̀ndøgoám; 'was' = ndøgoám; subordinate 'he was' = gegoam
kopo 1, menas 2, misika 3, then English loans foa, faev, siks, seven, eit, nain, ten, tuelv; numeral after the noun ('ezoqa menas' two people); 'about N' = 'ande āv N ndi꞉gú'
-qa after a verb stem = purpose ('in order to')
-ak on a place or group = person/people of (Izlael-ak; 'Itiopia manqei-ák' an Ethiopian; 'Asa khagua bawan-ák' of the tribe of Asher)
'also / even X' = 'até <X>-a'; 'only' = mba after the word
a place name takes a class noun: <name> vemiav (village), <name> taon (town), <name> manqei (land), <name> plovins (province)
acute, grave, macron, circumflex (questions) and U+1DC4 (prohibitives) mark tone and mood; headings carry no tone marks; U+A789 (꞉) is part of some prefixes
entries.note: Copy tone marks from the model verse; forms built by analogy carry uncertain tones.

entries.value: poetry as //1 / //2 lines where the BSB has poetry (Magnificat)
r → l; r before a consonant drops
j → z
th → t
initial h drops
ch, k → k
vowels follow the English pronunciation of the name (Deivid, Eibleem, Aezek, Izip, Izlael)
the oath 'thus may the LORD do to me and more' has no NT model; rendered as two plain sentences (only death shall part us; if anything else does, may the LORD punish me)
no NT word for sister-in-law (husband's brother's wife); 'qogu ezoqam' (your female relative) used
no 'call me X' imperative attested; rendered as 'my name shall be X' after the Luke 1:60 pattern
no passive 'I will be buried' with a 1sg patient; rendered nominally 'my grave will be there' (manqei ozu)
'the LORD has testified against me' rendered as 'spoke about/against me' (Mat 12:32 frame); other readings (afflicted, humbled) possible
'I went away full' has no NT word for 'full' of a person; rendered 'with my family'; 'empty' as khakha-mbá (empty-handed)
'would you refrain from having husbands' and 'wait for them to grow up' built from kewag (wait) and khouwev (grow) without a close model
'beginning of the barley harvest' paraphrased 'people began reaping the barley crops'; whether avøe alone means harvest is unknown
the prohibitive 'do not urge me' was built on the stem pouwe by the tone pattern; tones unverified
חֶסֶד: tanakh matev (mercy, compassion) chosen over kuku matev (love, grace); both frequent
the glossary spells the person Lut (Mat 1:5) but the project's book title is Rut; the text uses Lut

narrative-past subject prefixes on the verb: ge- (he), gu- (she), gi- (they), qa- (it); gu- also when a man acts on a woman; a plural subject wins. The forms with U+A789 (gu꞉-, gunu꞉-) are not feminine: they are a durative/locative 'be at, be in, be doing' used with any subject (Peter sitting, Jesus walking through the fields, God remaining in us)
entries.note: Refines chapter 1's open question 10: the gender reading holds for plain gu- (gu-ewag, gui-ova, gunøwav), not for gu꞉-/gunu꞉-.

entries.value: 2sg past prefix qoqo- (you did, you came, you put, you were); qoqonø- = you (sg) acting on me; qoqombøe-/qoqombo- = you on him/her; qoqote- before some stems (you said)

prohibition by a tone pattern on the verb: grave on the penult and the rising mark (U+1DC4) on the last vowel, object prefix kept. Attested 2sg forms: 'do not walk/go' (1Ti 5:21), 'do not leave her' (1Co 7:12); 2pl with a 3sg object: 'do not give him' (Eph 4:30), 'touch not' (2Co 6:17); negative wish with be- and the same marks: 'may it not happen to you' (Mat 16:22)
entries.note: 299 distinct prohibitive forms in the NT; prefer an attested one over building.

entries.value: wishes and blessings with be-: bezø- (for them), betaqa- (for you sg: 'may it be yours', 'may it not happen to you'), bè- plus an object-marked stem ('may this man be blessed'); 'continue to' = até be-
an order or command is framed with manqa/manqat + løvua carrying the subject and object prefixes, then quoted as direct speech (or as 'av nqægo' content)
a polite request opens with Ambá and its verb takes the suffix -ɨn; 'you may / you can' = 'qo kopømbaqapé, toqo-<verb>'
'where' = gekham-tē before the verb, which carries a macron; 'whose' = gekha ezoqam- with the possessive suffix of the possessed and a circumflex (-gû, -qâ); 'Gê,' also opens wh-questions

an agent noun is a verb stem or nominal plus ezoqam: field-keeping person (tenant), water-giving person (waterer), sowing person (sower), word-speaking person (prophet), work person (servant, worker, harvester)
qanaqanus (morning), khøuwa muin (noon), khagus (evening), lova (night), nqægo khaiya (today), atema ndakin (until now); 'from morning to evening' = qanaqanus atéma khagus

commands: 2sg forms attested as such for the common verbs: go (Mòqoqáv, qanøqáv), come (Qotøndéqāv, vø̀ndoqáv), eat (mòqológ), sit/stay (qanøqóm), take off / pull out (vø̀khofoé, vø̀khæ-khofoém pl); 2pl tozo-/sozó-/zøtø-/mòzo-; 1pl hortative bizi-; future-as-command Soqóqaváq

no NT word for gleaning (לקט) or for reapers; gleaning rendered as the NT's 'pick heads of grain' (bali nanga vingisam, after wit nanga ndøvingisømém) and harvesters as sasae ezoqam (workers), as Mat 13:30 does
no noun for a sheaf or bundle of cut grain; 'bali møvøyam' built from 'tie in bundles' and 'barn' (Mat 13:30)
no term for the kinsman-redeemer (גֹּאֵל); described as 'one of our relatives who are there to redeem us' with the NT's redeem verb (nqovotaz)
no word for refuge; 'taken refuge under his wings' made concrete as 'you came to him and put yourself under his wings' (taf mokho-te, Luk 13:34; 'put into my hand', Luk 19:20)
the ephah (about 22 litres) rendered 'about one yakhav' (basket, and the NT's unit for measures of oil); the NT also writes litres with digits (100 litás, Jhn 2:6)
'roasted grain' as bali nanga vesu; vesu (broiled) is attested once, of fish
no word for a foreman; 'the servant who was set over the harvesters' described as the servant who looked after the other workers (kewag)

'she ate and was satisfied': ewez with a singular personal object (mbo-) is attested only as 'grew weary/aggravated' (Jhn 4:6, Act 16:18); the plural (zø-ewez) means 'were filled'; the singular 'filled' sense is assumed
'stay close to / keep with' (דבק) in the imperative rendered 'namba mba qanøqóm' (stay only with); narrative 'clung to' keeps chapter 1's built gùmu-tøkenøvém
no word for chance ('she happened to come'); rendered 'it turned out thus:' (matev āv qanefakhán nqǽgo)
'the LORD bless you' and 'blessed be he' use the NT's khakheinøv (bless, make well); the 2sg optative bèkhakheinøqavém is built from bèkhakheinøvém and tø̀khakheinøqavém
'do not rebuke her' built on gugu (rebuke) by the prohibitive tone rule (mbogùgu᷄); not attested

a rhetorical 'is it not / am I not' question is 'Gê, <statement with the negative verb (-eâv) or mbà>?' with the circumflex, usually followed by its own answer (Gê, no Yesu ometeâv? No mø̀e-omét.); a 'should not' question may become a plain statement (Luk 13:16)
entries.note: Rut 3:1 'should I not seek a resting place for you' is rendered as a statement of intent

entries.value: after a first command, further commands chain with vø̀-/vø̄- + stem without a subject prefix (Mòqo-itán, ibøkha iz vø̄ndap, neka Evezøza vømbō-akha; Mòqo-itán, neka venanqei nonqo vø̄løvøen); a sentence-initial vø̀-command carries a grave and a final acute (vø̀khofoé, vø̀takhaém)
entries.note: Rut 3:3-4 and 3:13 build vø̀sungúz, vø̄qouz, vø̄sømbiam / vø̀sømbiám on this pattern; vø̄-uz and vø̀khofoé are attested as such

entries.value: 3sg negative future = ge-/gemǿ- (+ object prefix) + stem with a high tone + -ák (gétayák 'will not hold', gembótakák 'will not let', gemǿ-navøemák 'will never end'); 1pl zí-...-ák, 1sg nó-...-ák; a generic 'no one will / does know' = Ezoqa mè꞉-otevák

'if X (does)' = irrealis verb + tøgoat / tegoat ('if he intends to leave' = ivøve-qa tegoat); 'if he does not X' = X-eav tøgoat (tøkeeav tøgoat, okɨeav tøgoat); 'if he wants (to X)' = (X-qa) poev tømbogoat; 'if not' = Mbain tøgoat; the apodosis follows with yaq; 'if so' = Av toqotegoat ndægo

'A exceeds B' = A, B mø̀ndøløvú (A is greater than B: God is greater than our heart); 'he far surpasses me' = ndego no ùnime꞉-løvúmb; the respect compared is added as taqa yaq-te or noqa ... mø̀ndøløvú
entries.note: used in Rut 1:13 (more bitter), 3:10 (more kindness than before), 3:12 (a nearer redeemer)

entries.value: qanaqanus (morning), khøuwa muin (noon), khagus (evening), lova (night), nqægo lova (tonight), qamø-umba / lova u-mba (midnight), qanaqanus lovølova-ús (early morning while still dark), khøuwa qandopave (day broke), atema꞉ vøndōpave (until daybreak), nqægo khaiya (today), atema ndakin (until now); 'from morning to evening' = qanaqanus atéma khagus

a locative relative is bracketed 'ma … ndøgo' (where …); with a head noun the head comes first and the ma-clause follows: 'ta manqei ndøgo, ma <clause>' (the place where …); a person is characterised by an appositive clause after the name, 'ndego <clause>,' (Jhn 18:26: the man whose ear Peter cut off)
entries.note: Rut 1:7, 2:3, 3:4 (place), Rut 3:2 (Boaz, with whose girls you worked)

entries.value: no NT word for a threshing floor; 'bali evem nonqo' (barley-winnowing place) built on the NT's 'wit evem nonqo' (Luk 3:17); winnow = evem
no word for a heap or pile of grain; 'bali nqeitam' (stored / piled barley) built from nqeit (put in, store: barn, fill baskets); 'at the end of the heap' = bali nqeitam-qa vaev-te
no 'as the LORD lives' formula; rendered with the NT's swearing frame 'I swear to the LORD thus:' (no Evezøza-te, āv qaté-unimanqatín nqǽgo:), which loses 'lives'

'let him redeem you' (betaqá-nqovotáz) and 'I will redeem you' (søtaqá-nqovotáz) are built from the optative betaqa- and the 1sg-to-2sg future søtaqá- (Søtaqá-etoám) on the stem nqovotaz; the kinsman-redeemer himself stays a description (gap:kinsman_redeemer)

'six measures (seahs) of barley' rendered 'bali yakhav siks' with the NT's unit yakhav (basket, measure), the same word used for the ephah in Rut 2:17; the real quantity (about 40 litres) is not conveyed

the rhetorical 'should I not seek a resting place for you?' has no close model as a 1sg deontic question; rendered as a statement of intent 'No qo-te pusup manqei vawa-qa nombogó' (I want to seek …), with vawa-qa nombogó built after 'yoge-qa nombogó' (Act 25:22)

'spread the corner of your garment over me' rendered as the request 'Ambá qoqa ndabua-te qonø-gutavɨ́n' (please cover me with your garment), built from the request frame 'Ambá ibøkha qonø-etoamɨ́n' (Jhn 4:7) and gutav (cover); the 'wing' reading (taf, Rut 2:12) was not used
no word for 'startled'; 'Boaz was startled' rendered as two sentences, 'Boaz woke up' (gesuzam, Act 16:27) and 'Trembling.' (Kha wageap-ús, Luk 8:47)

'How did it go, my daughter?' (Hebrew 'who are you?') rendered 'Gê, áv khané꞉go, qo-te?' (how is it with you) after 'Gê, áv khané꞉go, …' (how is it that …, Act 2:8); the circumflex / question tone of the built phrase is unverified

'lie down' is the sleep stem sømbi (sømbiam); attested: sasa ndøsømbiam, gesømbimám (he lay), ginø-sømbiám; built: gusømbimám (she lay, 3:8, 3:14), genø-sømbiám (he lay down, 3:7), the imperatives vø̄sømbiam / vø̀sømbiám (3:4, 3:13), 'when he lies down' = sømbiam-qa tewav (3:4)

'do not let the man know you are there' and 'do not let it be known that a woman came' have no jussive-passive model; rendered with the negative future 'X mè꞉-otevák' (X will / must not notice, know; 1Co 2:11 'no one knows')

'he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today' rendered 'pusa gétayák, atema nqanek manqat nqægo khaiya vømǿ-navøēm' (he will not rest until he has finished this matter today); gétayák is attested only in 'yaq-fia gétayák' (will not hold judgment)

the redeemer as a character in narrative (Rut 4:1, 3, 6, 8) = 'ta ekeza ezoqam ndøgo' (that relative), introduced in 4:1 by 'Boaz teqa yaq-te manqat ge-ein' (of whom Boaz had spoken); 'to redeem' = nqovotaz, 'right of redemption' = nqovotaz matev (built), 'I will redeem' = nó-nqovotáz (built after nó-unimanqatín Heb 8:8), imperative gè-nqovotáz (built after gè-etoám Luk 6:38)

the narrator's note on an old custom has no NT model of a habitual past; rendered 'Ibugukhokhof, Izlael manqei-te, matev nqánek ndøgoám:' + a conditional case (tegoat ... yaq) + Heb 6:16 'ndigu ekeza manqat gè-unimanqatinimín' for the confirmation; 'exchange' merged into wi

'raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance' rendered as a wish 'ta ezoqam-qa iz, ndego genanim, teqa manqei-te nango begó' (may the dead man's name be on his land again); Luk 20:28 'patu bembō-qatayat' (raise up offspring for him) is the closer levirate model but has a 3sg subject; 'his name will not be cut off' = teqa iz ... gemǿ-navøemák (after Luk 1:33)
'tell me' (2sg imperative with 1sg addressee) = Qonømbé-eīn (Act 22:27); 'tell us' = Soqoní-eín (Act 5:8); 'I am telling you' = no qo ... nqataqa-manqate (2Ti 2:7)
entries.note: Rut 4:4

entries.value: human: the oath becomes a promise with a self-curse: 'I promise this; if I do not keep it, the LORD may - let him strike me' (formula:oath_may_the_lord_punish), after 'only death will separate us' (formula:only_death_parts)
words: anything but death separates you and me
entries.note: Ours: two plain sentences. The human keeps the curse as an optative of ngi (strike) on 1sg.

entries.value: human: 'your brother-in-law's wife', kin noun qakhapikia (husband's brother) + -pakha + -gu zas (term:H2994)
entries.note: Ours: 'qogu ezoqam' (your female relative).

entries.value: human: prohibitive pl with 1sg object for 'do not call me X', then a 2pl future for 'call me Y' (formula:call_me), each followed by the name's meaning (formula:explain_name)
entries.note: Ours: 'my name shall be X' (Luk 1:60).

entries.value: human: the 1sg future of otamb (bury) carries the passive sense: 'there I will be buried' (term:H6912.h); no passive construction needed
entries.note: Ours: 'my grave will be there'.

entries.value: human: 'testified against me' and 'afflicted me' are merged into one clause, 'the LORD has ruined my life' (ngi strike + yage life, 1:21); 1:13 'the hand of the LORD has gone out against me' = 'the LORD has struck me' (gènøngiú)
words: the hand of the lord has gone out against me
entries.note: Ours: 'spoke against me' (Mat 12:32). Merging two parallel Hebrew clauses is a human pattern (see ot-narrative.md).

entries.value: human: 'full' and 'empty' of a person = with and without husband and sons: 'with my husband and my sons' (-ús having) ... 'no husband, no children' (mbaín)
entries.note: Ours: 'with my family' / khakha-mbá. 'empty-handed' of goods = 'zenda-zenda mba' (RUT 3:17, term:H7387.h).

entries.value: human: 'would you wait many years until these children grow up? Would you go on living as widows until my sons marry you?' (kewag wait + atema until; ngængæm widows, term:widows)
words: wait for them to grow up
entries.note: Ours: built from kewag and khouwev; close to the human.

entries.value: human: 'the barley-picking season began' (bali vingisam viav, term:H7105.h), plus an explanation of barley in brackets at the end of the verse
entries.note: Ours: 'people began reaping the barley crops' (avøe). The harvest is a season (viav), not avøe gigiap.

entries.value: human: our built prohibitive was right in its tone pattern; the human form has the rising mark on the last vowel followed by the stem's final -t: 'do not urge me' (RUT 1:16)
entries.note: Ours lacked the final consonant. See prohibitive.3.

entries.value: human: human kindness = good deeds (matev mbomømboma, Ruth), God's loving devotion = kuku matev (Jonah); see term:H2617.h
entries.note: Ours: tanakh matev. tanakh is the human's word for favour and pity.

entries.value: human: Lut throughout; the 2015 book heading is also 'Lut'
entries.note: Decided: Lut for the person and the book.

entries.value: human: gleaning = picking up the left-over barley (bali khakhayakh + pisam/pisum, term:H3950.h); harvesters = sasae ezoqam (workers), as ours
entries.note: Ours: 'bali nanga vingisam' (pluck heads of grain).

entries.value: human: the sheaves are 'the barley stalks being tied' (bali løvøtap, term:H6016.h); 2:7 'among the sheaves' is left out
entries.note: Ours: 'bali møvøyam'.

entries.value: human: the redeemer is 'X's relative' (ekeza ezoqam); his duty is explained in 2:20 from the law of Moses ('a woman whose husband dies, the husband's relative must help her'); redeeming = buying the land (wi) and marrying the widow (okɨ); see term:H1350.h
entries.note: Ours: 'relatives who are there to redeem us' with the NT's nqovotaz. The human adds the background inside the text.

entries.value: human: the image is dropped: 'you have come to him for help' (tøke-qa ... te-te), formula:repay_your_work
entries.note: Ours: made concrete with taf (wings). The human renders the meaning, not the picture.

entries.value: human: the measure is converted to kilograms in the text: 'about 10 kilograms' (term:H374.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'about one yakhav' (basket). Same for the seah (term:H5429.h).

entries.value: human: bali lonqotøvap (term:H7039)
entries.note: Ours: 'bali nanga vesu'.

entries.value: human: 'the man who looked after the workers' (kewag), as ours (term:H5324)
entries.note: Ours confirmed.

entries.value: human: 'it (the food) filled her' = qa- + mbo- + ewez (term:H7646.h)
entries.note: Ours: open between mbo- and zø-; the human uses the inanimate subject qa-.

entries.value: human: 'stay here with ...' = 'be (go) here' + namba (formula:stay_with.h); 'clung to her' = 'stayed, with Naomi' (term:H1692.h); 'stayed close to the girls' = 'worked beside them'
entries.note: Ours: 'namba mba qanøqóm', 'gùmu-tøkenøvém'.

entries.value: human: 'she happened to come to Boaz's field' = 'she did not know that this field was Boaz's' (formula:it_turned_out.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'it turned out thus:'.

entries.value: human: 'Yawe zenda ndò꞉vé qo-te' (may the LORD put his hand on you), term:H1288.h; no optative of khakheinøv
entries.note: Ours: built 2sg optative bèkhakheinøqavém.

entries.value: human: 'do not say a word to her about it' (prohibitive pl of ein), term:H1605.h
entries.note: Ours: built prohibitive of gugu.

entries.value: human: 'the grain-threshing place' (bali nanga tøkuza manqei, term:H1637.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'bali evem nonqo'; evem (winnow) itself is right (RUT 3:2).

entries.value: human: bali nanga møvøza (term:H6194.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'bali nqeitam'.

entries.value: human: 'I promise you before the LORD's face' (bugug-té qataqambø-manqaté), formula:as_the_lord_lives.h; 'lives' is not rendered
words: as surely as the lord lives
entries.note: Ours: 'I swear to the LORD thus:' (Act 23:14). Both lose 'lives'; the human frame is shorter.

entries.value: human: redeeming the widow = marrying her: 'if he wants to marry you, good, let him marry you' ... 'I will marry you' (okɨ with the 2sg object, formula:if_he_wants_good)
entries.note: Ours: built forms of nqovotaz.

entries.value: human: 'its weight was about 20 kilograms' (term:H5429.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'bali yakhav siks'.

entries.value: human: the rhetorical question becomes a statement of intent, as ours: 'I will find you a husband, so that you will live well' (term:H4494.h, term:H3190.h)
entries.note: Ours confirmed in form (statement), with the content made explicit (husband).

entries.value: human: 'take a little of your blanket and cover me' (khafu, term:H6566.h); then 'and look after me', 'please marry me' (No ambá qonøkeɨ́n)
words: spread the corner of your garment over me
entries.note: Ours: 'please cover me with your garment' (gutav). The human spells out the request's meaning.

entries.value: human: 'Boaz woke up, turned over, and fear took him' (tènesuzám ... nqova mbondáf, term:H2729.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'woke up' + 'trembling' - the same split into clauses.

entries.value: human: 'My daughter, how did things go (for you)?' (formula:how_did_it_go.h)
entries.note: Ours: 'how is it with you'.

entries.value: human: lie (down) = buv in all forms; sleep = venanqei buv (term:H7901.h)
entries.note: Ours: built forms of sømbi (sleep).

entries.value: human: the negative optative be- + prohibitive tone: 'let Boaz not see you', 'let no one know' (formula:not_let_the_man_know.h, feature negative_optative)
words: do not let the man know
do not let it be known
entries.note: Ours: negative future 'will not notice'.

entries.value: human: 'Boaz will not rest (pusa ... gétayák). The matter will be settled today.' - ours confirmed in the verb (formula:matter_settled)
entries.note: Ours confirmed (pusa gétayák).

entries.value: human: in narrative 'Elimelek-ge ekeza ezoqam' (Elimelech's relative) or 'ndego ezoqam' (that man), 4:1 'of whom Boaz had spoken to Ruth'
entries.note: Ours: 'ta ekeza ezoqam ndøgo' - close.

entries.value: human: 'In those days in Israel the custom was this:' + the case told with the -ɨn suffix (feature suffix_in) + 'This was the Israelites' custom' (formula:in_former_times)
words: to make any matter legally binding
entries.note: Ours: 'Ibugukhokhof ... matev nqánek ndøgoám:' + a conditional case; the human has a habitual suffix the NT-only agents did not know.

entries.value: human: 'that land will stay in the dead man's name' (4:5) and 'so Mahlon's name will not be forgotten among his people and in this town' (4:10, negative future of navøem)
words: raise up the name of the deceased
entries.note: Ours: a wish 'may the dead man's name be on his land again'.

entries.value: r → l (Lut, Lam, Pelez, Ezlon, Izlael, Mala, Laisol); r before a consonant drops (Opa, Tasis) and so does a final r (Tama)
entries.note: Confirmed by every r in Ruth/Jonah.

entries.value: j (Hebrew y) → z; Jo- → Zio- (Ziona Jonah, Ziopa Joppa, as NT Zion John)
h drops at the start (Ezlon) and inside a name (Malon, Nason); final -h drops (Zuda, Opa, Niniva, Eflat)
ch, k → k (Elimelek, Kilion)
entries.note: Confirmed.

entries.value: sh → s (Tasis Tarshish, Nason Nahshon)
ph → f (Eflat Ephrath)
double consonants are written single (Amitai Amittai, Ziopa Joppa, Aminadab Amminadab)

vowels: names the NT has keep the NT's English-sounding form (Deivid, Laisol, Zesi); names new in the OT stay close to the spelling (Naomi, not Neomi; Elimelek, Kilion, Amitai, Obed); Nineveh → Niniva
entries.note: The NT-only agents built Neomi and Eflata from the pronunciation rule; the human writes Naomi and Eflat. For a new OT name: BSB spelling + the consonant rules, NT form where the NT has the name.

entries.value: in the 2015 OT a possessed kin noun takes -pakha (pl -pakha-za): zakhapuka-pakha (her mother-in-law), ziwap-pakha / ziupim-pakha-za (daughter(s)-in-law), sæ-pakha (my daughter), anganeam-pakha (husband), yo-pakha (son), qakhapikia-pakha (brother-in-law); the stem can change with the possessor's person (z- her, q- your: zakhapuka / qakhapuka, zøvøndipakha / qavøndipakha). The NT has -pakha only in evøndipakha (parents)
entries.note: New: the NT-only agents never saw it (their drafts have bare kin nouns). Whether the newer NT revision dropped -pakha or the NT simply has no such contexts is a question for the Kuni team.

entries.value: narrative links a new event to the last one by repeating it as a backgrounded clause (often closed by ndøgo, or followed by yaq): 'they settled there. And while they lived in Moab, Elimelech died'; 'they came to Bethlehem. When they came to Bethlehem ...'; 'Naomi said this, and they wept'
entries.note: The human adds such links where the Hebrew has none (1:3, 1:14, 3:5, JON 2:2). See ot-narrative.md.

entries.value: the translators make implicit information explicit inside the text: the cause of a famine (RUT 1:1), the meaning of names (1:20), an unfamiliar plant in brackets (1:22 barley), the law behind the redeemer (2:20), the place of council at the gate (4:1), measures converted to kilograms (2:17, 3:15), the purpose of a request (3:9 'please marry me'), the resting place as a husband (3:1), lots as a procedure (JON 1:7)
entries.note: Drafts may do the same; mark each addition in the chapter notes for the team's review.

entries.value: Hebrew images are rendered by their meaning: 'under whose wings you have taken refuge' = 'you have come to him for help'; 'the hand of the LORD has gone out against me' = 'the LORD has struck me'; 'cannot tell right from left' = 'do not know which way is good'; 'spread your wing over me' = 'cover me ... please marry me'

a negative wish or indirect prohibition ('let him not', 'let no one') is be- + the prohibitive tone (grave on the penult, U+1DC4 on the last vowel): 'let Boaz not see you', 'let no one know', 'let them not eat or drink'
entries.note: New: the NT-only agents used a negative future instead. NT model: Mat 16:22 (prohibitive.2).

entries.value: prohibition by a tone pattern on the verb: grave on the penult and the rising mark (U+1DC4) on the last vowel, object prefix kept; a final consonant follows the mark (pòuwe᷄t, qàva᷄q, khafène᷄m, eìni᷄m, akhàya᷄m). 2sg: 'do not urge me', 'do not go', 'do not be afraid', 'do not go back'; 2pl: 'do not drive her away', 'do not say a word to her', 'do not call me', 'do not eat or drink'; 1pl object: 'do not give us death' (JON 1:14). Negative wish: be- + the same marks (negative_optative)
entries.note: The rule the NT-only agents used is confirmed by nine OT stems; their 'nøpòuwe᷄' lacked the stem's final t. NT: 299 distinct prohibitive forms; prefer an attested one.

entries.value: 1pl 'let us' = zí- / sizi- / qazinǿ- on the verb (NT bizi-): 'let us write', 'let us put', 'let us see', 'let us wait', 'let us fast'; 'we will go' (future 1pl) = qazinǿ-
entries.note: The NT has bizi- (Luk 2:15 'Bìziniáv'); zí-/sizi- forms were not in the store.

entries.value: commands: 2sg mò-/qo-/qa- (+ -nø- thither, -ndo- hither): 'go there' qonǿqáv, 'go' Mòqoqáv / Vø̀qáv, 'come here' Qotøndéqāv, 'eat' qólóg / mòqológ, 'sit' Qànøqóm, 'get up' Mòqosuzám, 'hold it' Qóvøndáz, 'lie down' sasa qóbūv, 'buy it' ndøwí; 2pl qazonǿ- / zó- / vø̀- / qànø- ...-m/-v/-n: 'go back' Qazonǿ-qavøním, 'sit down' Qànøqonáv, 'pull out' zó-ovobém, 'wear' zó-uzám, 'turn' Zóqambúz; a following command chains with vø̀-/vø̄-; 1pl hortative zí-/sizi-/bizi- (hortative)

the verb suffix -ɨn marks a non-actual event: a polite request with Ambá ('please let me go'), a wished or attempted act with amba ('I wanted to flee', 'the ship nearly broke up'), a hypothetical ('even if you had seven sons, they could not help you as ...'), and a customary act in a description of custom (RUT 4:7) or a repeated act (RUT 2:7)
entries.note: Refines request_permission (NT: Ambá ... -ɨn); the habitual use answers gap:custom_explanation. The NT glossary uses it for customs too ('gingazemɨn', Keliso).

entries.value: 'can / may' = kopømbá (it is fine, possible) / kopømbaqapé; 'cannot' = kopømba mbaín + irrealis verb; 'if he refuses, fine' = '..., kopømbá'

'if X' = irrealis verb (te-/tu-/toqo-/tæ- ...) + tøgoat/tegoat, then yaq; 'if he does not' = X-eav tøgoat ('poeveav tøgoat' if he does not want); 'if he wants to X' = irrealis of poev + irrealis X ('tømbopoe teqakɨ'); 'if so / if I do that' = 'Av tægoat ndægo, yaq ...'; 'even if' = 'Até ndøgó-a, ...'; 'when you buy' = 'Geté ... toqondap' (irrealis without tøgoat)
entries.note: Confirmed and extended by Ruth 3-4 (legal conditions).

entries.value: the frame precedes the quote: speaker (addressee) + frame verb with person and object prefixes, then “...”. In Ruth/Jonah most frames are the short verb (gumbo-ein to her, gezø-ein to them); a reply takes -ndo-/-ndu- (gundu-ein, gendo-ein, gindu-einim); the long 'āv ... nqǽgo' frame marks questions, prayers, orders and solemn speech. A frame may follow a hearing clause ('Ruth heard this and replied'). Quotes inside quotes take ‘ ’
entries.note: Style figure: 'nqǽgo' 11.4 per 1000 words in Ruth, 7.7 in Jonah (NT Gospels+Acts 10.6).

entries.value: a vocative stands first as its own sentence; a name in the vocative moves its accent to the first syllable (Evézøza, Zíona; NT Méli); kin and titles: Sǽ-pakha (my daughter), Nogí sæ-pakha-za (my daughters), Khanánqa (sir)

interjections open the reply as their own sentence: Nqáe! (look), Áe, (there, behold, in narrative), Yáiyé! (joy, surprise), Tiá. (no!), Mbaín. (no), Āv taoká. (not so), Ság. (good, enough), Qanimáv. (good, yes, agreed), Unimanqatín. (truly), Éisa, (perhaps)
entries.note: The human adds them where the Hebrew has none (Yáiyé in 2:20 and 4:17, Qanimáv in 3:5, 4:4, 4:11).

entries.value: 'like X' = 'av X ndi꞉gu / ngi꞉gu' after the compared clause; 'as if' = andé; 'as you said' = 'av ... ndægo'

a relative clause follows its head, opened by the pronoun of the head (ndego, ndugu, ndigu) and closed by the verb: 'Naomi, the woman who came back from Moab'; 'the man who looked after the workers'; 'a woman whose husband dies'; 'God, who lives in heaven'
entries.note: Complements relative_clause.2 (locative ma ... ndøgo).

entries.value: Yaq opens most narrative sentences (50 per 1000 words in Ruth, 60 in Jonah; NT 44); vø̄- chains following actions without subject marking and 'sasa nd(ø)-' closes the chain; 'até gendego, ...' (he for his part, then he) opens a new action of a known participant; Geté = but (8.5/1000); 'Zapa ndǿgo,' (because) is rare (1.8 Ruth, 2.3 Jonah; NT 3.4, our drafts 5.2): most Hebrew כִּי clauses are not marked; neka joins less often than in the NT (13.6 vs 18.8); 'Yaq nakémbá' = therefore
entries.note: Figures from _eval/human_ruth_analysis.md section 2 (tone marks ignored).

entries.value: short sentences: 9.0 words per sentence in Ruth, 8.7 in Jonah (NT Gospels+Acts 9.9); about 1.6 Hebrew clauses per Kuni sentence; a long Hebrew verse becomes 3-6 sentences; a key clause can be repeated at the end of the verse (1:1 'Vikia sekeqape ndømát.'); names, attributes and time phrases stand as sentences of their own ('Khøuwa kopó.' JON 3:4; 'Khøuwa misiká neka lova misika.' JON 2:1)

a time setting opens the sentence: 'Qàgoám.' opens a book; 'Ta khøuwa-te ndøgo, …' (in those days), 'Khøuwa nøme,' (one day), 'Yaq ta lova ndøgo,' (that night), 'Taqa zita-te,' (afterwards); a subordinate time clause ends in ndøgo ('when it was time to eat')

kopo 1, menas 2, misika 3, then English loans (foa, faev, siks, seven, ten, foti 40); large numbers as English words (wan andled tuenti taosen 120,000); measures in digits with kilogrém; numeral after the noun (ezoqa menas, viav ten); 'about N' = 'ande āv N ndægó'

verb-final (SOV) clauses, but phrases of company, place and time often follow the verb as afterthoughts ('he went to live in Moab, with his wife and two sons'; 'they went back to Judah, with the daughters-in-law'); a short clause per event
entries.note: The afterthoughts are why lexeme-aligner's order profile measures Hebrew V>O kept 58% (cop:order).

entries.value: 'tell me' = Qonømbé-eīn (Act 22:27); 'tell us' = Qonimbí-eīn (JON 1:8; NT Soqoní-eín, Act 5:8); 'tell me (so I may know)' = 'sègenø-eín' (RUT 4:4)
gram-struct: postpositions (WALS 85A, external, confidence 0.99); its own alignment statistic (derived) says 'mixed' (52% after, n=5,381) and that adpositions are separate words in 68%
entries.external_source: lexeme-aligner gram-struct/external (WALS, CC-BY-4.0) and gram-struct/derived (kvg_wbt), CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 basis
entries.note: Agrees with our adposition entry and adds the WALS code. The derived 'mixed' disagrees with ours: Kuni writes most postpositions as hyphenated suffixes (-te) and has free relational nouns (namba, mokho-te, zita-te) that the aligner may count on either side; trust WALS + the corpus here.

entries.value: constituent-order profile (Ruth + Jonah, 130 verses, MACULA phrase roles): Hebrew order kept for o>v 70%, pp>v 68%, s>v 65%, v>o 58%, v>pp 61%, v>s 48%, v>v 71%; mean drift: verbs move later (+0.03), subjects and phrases earlier
entries.external_source: lexeme-aligner constituent-order-profile (kvg_wbt, Ruth+Jonah), CC0 statistics on a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 basis
entries.note: Adds a measured figure; it seems to disagree with verb-final order (V>O kept 58%) but does not: Kuni breaks a Hebrew clause into several short clauses and puts company, place and time after the verb (constituent_order.2), so a Hebrew object can align to a later clause. Measured on the test books themselves.

entries.value: target-morphology (unsupervised, 14,101 types): top prefixes vø-, qa-, ndø-, ge-, gi-, te-, tø-, ti-, gè-, be-, qo-, mø-, zø-, nø-, gu-; top suffixes -m, -t, -am, -at, -o, -át, -ɨn, -áv, -ák, -eáv
entries.external_source: lexeme-aligner target-morphology (kvg), CC0 statistics on a CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 basis
entries.note: Agrees with our verb prefixes (subject ge-/gu-/gi-, sequence vø-, optative be-, object zø-/nø-) and negation (-áv, -eáv, -ák). It adds -ɨn as one of the commonest suffixes (feature suffix_in). It treats tone-marked variants as separate affixes (-am / -ám) and cannot tell prefix chains apart, so use it as a check, not as a parser.

entries.value: ordinals are verbs of becoming: '<noun>, gè-<N>-éz' (the Nth angel, Rev 8:8; 'gèmbo-menas-éz' the second seal, Rev 6:3), 'khøuwa mø̀ndømø-<N>-éz' (it is the Nth day, Luk 24:21), 'khøuwa timømbo-misika-ez ndøgo' (on the third day, Luk 9:22); 'first' = bugukhokhof before the noun (Rev 8:7)
entries.note: The prefix chain varies (mø̀ndømbo- with foa, Jhn 11:39). formula:nth_day.

entries.value: a third-person wish or 'let it ...' for things also takes bete-/betø- + stem: 'let both grow' (Mat 13:30 bete-umianét), 'let your light shine' (Mat 5:16 betekháev); beside be- + stem (begó, befakhan, beqatøzo)
entries.note: Refines optative.2 for non-human subjects (the Gen 1 jussives).
